correctedHandover.correction: The route reads NO file and substitutes NOTHING: it POSTs request.body.prompt verbatim to {url}/prompt. The "%prompt%"/"%seed%" replacement is client-side (public/scripts/extensions/stable-diffusion/index.js:4216-4300, generateComfyImageCommon), which is why the workflows directory is not seeded for these scenarios and why every recorded prompt body is byte-identical to the request member.

mechanism: The upstream base URL comes from `request.body.url`, so no provider seam exists or is needed: the probe points it at `<mock>`, boots the pinned server unmodified, replaces its `node-fetch` module and the global `fetch` with a controlled peer, and records every outbound request the pinned handler would have sent. The Go replay turns `<mock>` into its own httptest listener and applies the same substring+times rule selection the stub uses (AGENTS rule 20).

fields.reason: the pinned handler chooses 200/400/500 itself for every branch
res.send(object) is JSON while res.send(string) is html; content-length and ETag are recomputed from the recorded body on both sides
the {format,data} projection with member order, and every fixed error message
the body is a V8 engine message (a property-read TypeError and a JSON.parse SyntaxError); nulled with its derived content-length/ETag, and the status plus the outbound count stay compared
the escaped target is endpoint behaviour: the raw id interpolation into /history/<id> and the /view special-query encoding
POST /prompt and POST /run versus three GETs
the DECLARED header set: empty for all three comfy requests, exactly the bearer token for the runpod pair. Asserted in both directions by the test so an added Authorization fails
the verbatim prompt forward, the no-body case, and the runpod wrap/no-wrap/wrapped-undefined forms
THE POLL COUNT is the only thing that discriminates a cache-like shortcut from the real loop
synthetic peer answers with known digests; live provider content would be shape only

normalizations: The upstream origin is recorded as `<mock>`: the fixture holds no host and no port.
The prompt id and the runpod job id are synthetic constants chosen by the peer, not host-derived values.
Synthetic credentials and synthetic image bytes only.
notRecorded: the CANCEL leg: the pinned socket-close handler POSTs /interrupt (comfy) or /cancel/<jobId> (runpod) when the caller goes away. The probe peer answers every rule immediately, so there is never an in-flight generation whose caller can disappear; the Go behaviour is covered by a LABELLED implementation test with pinned parity UNOBSERVED (the A1111 precedent).

a url of `null` (urlJoin reads `.length` on it, a V8 message), a url that is an OBJECT or an ARRAY (urlJoin treats an array as a parts list), and a non-string prompt (node-fetch rejects a non-BodyInit) are NOT probed; GoTavern answers the urlJoin type message with the JavaScript String() form of the value, which is a recorded known difference for `null`.

the infinite branches are NOT probed: a history payload that never contains the id, a history entry that is falsy, and a runpod `output.images` that is empty all keep polling forever, exactly as pinned does. GoTavern keeps that inherited property (see the fixture note in the compat row) rather than adding a timeout the product does not have.

a url whose scheme is not http/https: `new URL` accepts it and node-fetch then refuses with "Only HTTP(S) protocols are supported", but the probe peer would answer it instead, so it is source-derived only. GoTavern answers "Invalid URL" there, which is a recorded known difference.
a /prompt JSON body that is not an object (`null`) and an `outputs` member that is missing both throw V8 messages; not probed.
timing is not recorded: the poll interval is a source-derived constant asserted by a labelled Go test, because a 100ms/500ms bucket cannot be discriminated from a fast host.
